note: Adverse second trip (recorded as eject-second-trip): the second pipe leaves the lip as the planar eject leaves it and lands in the trough where the first rests.

assumes.text: The second pipe starts at the state the planar eject-to-the-tip trial ends in: its place, speed and spin as it leaves the lip.
The robot stays docked; the withdrawal is tried in the planar eject trial. Only the lip and the official trough are surfaces.
The first pipe starts at rest where the nominal eject left it, in the same sector, square and centred with the second.
The official trough is cut at the section plane: its panel holes, the sector divider and the riser's 245 mm extent along the 302 mm pipe are not seen.
